title-info.book-title: NGINX JS DOM — Header and Body Filters

title.p: NGINX JS DOM — Header and Body Filters

section.p: NGINX JS DOM lets JavaScript code intercept and transform every HTTP response that passes through a location. The interception happens at two points in nginx’s filter chain:

Header filters — called once, just before response headers are sent to the client. The callback receives the live NginxRequest object and may mutate response headers in place. The filter is always synchronous.

Body filters — called for each piece of the response body (streaming modes) or once on the complete body (whole-body modes). Four execution modes cover every combination of sync/async and chunk/whole: wholeBodySync, wholeBodyAsync, streamingSync, streamingAsync.

Filters are registered per-location via methods on the NginxLocation object (accessible through nginx.http.servers[i].locations[j] or by iterating nginx.http.servers[i].locations). Registering a filter from any script that runs at config time — js_source, js_init_http, js_preprocess — is sufficient; the filter then applies to every request that reaches that location.
All filter management methods live on the NginxLocation object.

Both addHeaderFilter and addBodyFilter accept an optional second/third opts argument that controls where the new filter is inserted in the list:

stanza.v: name: string, // symbolic name — used by remove/get
before: fn | string, // insert immediately before this filter
after: fn | string, // insert immediately after this filter
index: number // insert at this absolute position (0-based)

section.p: Precedence (highest first): index > before / after > priority.
If before or after references a filter that does not exist, the new filter is appended.

stanza.v: const upper = function(req, body) { return body.toUpperCase(); };
// insert with a name so it can be removed later
const wrap = function(req, body) { return '[' + body + ']'; };
// priority-based ordering: lower numbers run first

section.p: Header filters are always synchronous. async function callbacks are accepted but any awaited operation completes after headers are already sent — do not rely on async behaviour inside a header filter.
The return value is ignored.
The body is accumulated from all nginx chain links until last_buf is seen. Then the JS filter chain runs once on the complete body string.

// throw new Error('...') → close the connection

section.p: Chaining: when multiple whole-body filters are registered they run in registration order; each filter receives the output of the previous one as its body argument.
Streaming filters run on each chunk individually as nginx delivers it. The filter chain processes chunks in registration order.

Output is produced via req.sendBuffer(data). Multiple calls per invocation are allowed; their output is concatenated in call order and forwarded downstream. The next filter in the chain receives the concatenated output of the previous filter — not the original chunk.

stanza.v: // no call to sendBuffer → chunk is dropped

section.p: flags is an object with one property:
flags.last — true if this is the last chunk (corresponds to nginx’s last_buf flag).
The filter returns a Promise. The resolved value determines the output:
Resolved value │ Effect
non-empty string │ Replace the chunk with this string
'' (empty string) │ Drop the chunk (emit nothing)
undefined / non-string │ Pass the chunk through unchanged
Rejection │ Close the connection with an error
req.sendBuffer() is not the output mechanism for streamingAsync — use the return value.

stanza.v: // return undefined / no return → pass through

section.p: Valid only inside a streamingSync filter callback. Appends data (coerced to string) to the current chunk’s output accumulator. Multiple calls per invocation are allowed.
If called outside a streamingSync context (i.e. inside a wholeBody* filter or outside any filter) it is a silent no-op and a WARN message is written to the error log.
Passed as the third argument to both streamingSync and streamingAsync callbacks:

stanza.v: last: boolean // true when this is the last chunk of the response

section.p: In mixed mode (see below) streaming filters receive the whole accumulated body as a single chunk with flags.last === true.

title.p: Mode selection (Mode A vs Mode B)

section.p: nginx JS DOM uses two internal dispatch strategies based on what filter types are registered for a location:
Mode │ When used │ Behaviour

Mode A — streaming │ Location has no wholeBody* filters │ nginx body-filter calls pass directly to the streaming chain; the body is never accumulated. Each call to nginx’s body filter = one call to each streaming filter.

Mode B — whole-body │ Location has at least one wholeBody* filter │ The body is fully accumulated, then ALL filters run in registration order on the complete body. streamingSync/streamingAsync filters in this list receive the whole body as a single last chunk.
The mode is selected automatically based on the filter list at request time. There is no explicit configuration knob.

title.p: Mixed mode (Mode B with streaming filters)

section.p: When both wholeBody* and streaming* filters share a location, Mode B is used and all filters run in registration order on the accumulated body. Streaming filters behave as follows:
streamingSync : called with (req, body, {last: true}). Emit output via req.sendBuffer(); no call → body is dropped.
streamingAsync : called with (req, body, {last: true}). Resolved string replaces the body; undefined passes through; '' drops it.

stanza.v: // Filter 2 (streaming): wrap in brackets — runs after filter 1

section.p: Filters execute in the order they appear in the location’s filter list. Both header and body filter lists are independent.

stanza.v: // Header filter runs first, body filters run in order for each request
const step1 = function(req, body) { return body.trim(); };
const step2 = function(req, body) { return body.toUpperCase(); };
const step3 = function(req, body) { return '[' + body + ']'; };
// body passes through step1 → step2 → step3 in that order

section.p: Filters can be added and removed at runtime from within a running filter callback. The implementation uses copy-on-write (COW) for the filter list: mutations during dispatch do not affect the current iteration but take effect for the next request.

// Remove a named filter while it is running (safe — COW guarantees
// the current dispatch sees the old list)

section.p: Filters added without an explicit index, before, or after option are inserted based on priority (lower = earlier, default 50):

stanza.v: // priority 10 runs before priority 20 runs before priority 50 (default)

section.p: Situation │ Behaviour
wholeBodySync filter throws │ Exception is logged; body is passed through unchanged; next filter runs.
wholeBodyAsync filter rejects │ Error is logged; connection is closed (HTTP 500 or connection reset).
streamingSync filter throws │ Exception is logged; chunk is dropped; next filter runs.
streamingAsync filter rejects │ Error is logged; connection is closed.
addBodyFilter / addHeaderFilter called with wrong type │ TypeError is thrown immediately (synchronous, propagates to the caller).

section.p: Method │ Returns │ Description
addHeaderFilter(fn [, opts]) │ undefined │ Register a header-filter callback.
addBodyFilter(mode, fn [, opts]) │ undefined │ Register a body-filter callback.
removeHeaderFilter(ref) │ undefined │ Remove a header filter by name or function reference.
removeBodyFilter(ref) │ undefined │ Remove a body filter by name or function reference.
getHeaderFilter(ref) │ {name, priority, fn} or null │ Retrieve header filter descriptor.
getBodyFilter(ref) │ {name, priority, fn, mode} or null │ Retrieve body filter descriptor.
headerFilters (getter) │ Array of {name, priority, fn} │ Snapshot of all header filters in dispatch order.
bodyFilters (getter) │ Array of {name, priority, fn, mode} │ Snapshot of all body filters in dispatch order.
Mode string │ Signature │ Output mechanism
'wholeBodySync' │ fn(req, body) → string|undefined │ Return value
'wholeBodyAsync' │ async fn(req, body) → Promise<string|undefined> │ Resolved value of returned Promise
'streamingSync' │ fn(req, chunk, flags) │ req.sendBuffer(data) — zero or more calls
'streamingAsync' │ async fn(req, chunk, flags) → Promise<string|undefined> │ Resolved value of returned Promise
Parameter │ Description
data │ String (or coercible to string) to append to the current chunk output.
Valid only inside a streamingSync callback. No-op + WARN log in all other contexts.
Property │ Type │ Description
name │ string │ Symbolic name for later remove / get calls. Optional.
priority │ number │ Insertion priority. Lower = earlier. Default 50. Used when no positional option (index, before, after) is given.
index │ number │ Absolute 0-based insertion position. Takes precedence over all other options.
before │ function or string │ Insert immediately before this filter (matched by function reference or name).
after │ function or string │ Insert immediately after this filter (matched by function reference or name).
Property │ Type │ Description
last │ boolean │ true if this is the final chunk of the response body.
